question.text: Standard deviation as a risk measure indicates:

answer.text: The average return of an investment
The exact future return of an investment
The volatility or dispersion of returns around the mean — higher values indicate more risk

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the NISM Series XV Research Analyst workbook (page 238), standard deviation is a statistical measure of risk based on the variability of returns around mean returns; higher dispersion implies higher risk. Pages 228 and 241 reinforce this by using standard deviation in the context of return volatility and risk-adjusted return measurement (for example, in the Sharpe ratio denominator). The Trap: Option B is wrong because standard deviation does not predict exact future returns; it summarises historical variability around the mean. Options A and D describe an average return or a guaranteed minimum, neither of which is what standard deviation measures. Note: Treat standard deviation purely as a dispersion measure - higher values mean wider swings around the mean and therefore higher risk, not higher or lower expected returns.
